# Harbour lights go dark

The harbour authority switched off its navigation lights for three hours on Tuesday night, after a routine update reached the wrong controllers and left the whole eastern channel unlit.

Pilots brought two cargo ships in by radar and by radio, and nobody was hurt, although a ferry waited outside the breakwater until the engineers had restored the lights and tested them.

The authority said the update had been meant for a small test rig, and that a mistake in the address list had sent it to every controller on the eastern side of the harbour at once.

Engineers restored the lights by hand, one controller at a time, and the authority has since split its address list in two so that test updates cannot reach the live network again.

The national regulator has asked for a written account of the incident by the end of the month, and it said it would decide then whether a formal inquiry into the update process was needed.
